The instant appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company for (O&Mnational Insc. Comp vs Savitri Devi And Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12204539/
1 setting aside the award dated 05.12.2006 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fatehabad (for short, 'the Tribunal')
 Tribunal'), whereby the claimants were awarded compensation of Rs.90,000/-
 Rs. along with interest @ 9% per annum.
FACTS NOT IN DISPUTE 2.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 15.11.2004 at about 3.00 pm, Satish Kumar had come to the shop of one Om Parkash son of Tara Chand resident of Dhani Majra.
He was standing in front of the shop after parking his bicycle.

In the meantime, a Haryana Roadways bus bearing registration No.
No.HR-62/0285 belonging to Fatehabad Fatehabad Depot came there.

It was being driven rashly and 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132930 FAO-312-2007 2007 (O&M) -2- negligently by Balwant Singh and it struck against Satish and dragged him and his bicycle up to some distance by coming on the wrong side of the ro road.
d. As a result, result Satish Kumar died at the spot due to the injuries received by him in the accident.
accident
After ter the accident, respondent No.1 had fled away from the spot leaving the bus there.
This occurrence was witnessed by Bansi Lal father of the deceased and Om Parkash.

3. From the pleading of the parties, the Tr Tribunal ibunal framed the following issues:-
"1.
Whether the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Bus No. HR-62/0285 0285 by respondent No.1?OPP 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 3. Whether the respondent N No.1 was not holding a valid and effective ective driving license at the time of the accident?
If so so,, to what effect?

OPR 4. Relief."
4.

After taking into consideration the pleadings and the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.
Rs.90,000/-,, along with interest @ 9% % per annum and further Insurance company was held liable to indemnify the insured i.e. the owner of the vehicle vehicle.
Hence, the Insurance Company filed the present appeal.

SUBMISSIONS OF THE COUNSEL FOR THE PARTIES (O&Mnational Insc. Comp vs Savitri Devi And Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12204539/
2 5.

The learned counsel cou for the appellant appellant-Insurance Company contends contend that the finding of the learned Tribunal is erroneous since the driving licence of the 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132930 FAO-312-2007 2007 (O&M) -3- driver was valid from 17.11.2004,
17.11.2004 whereas, the accident took place on 15.11.2004. Therefore, on the date of accident, the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.
He further contended that the licence was not renewed and it was the responsibility of the Haryana Roadways, who was to see the driving of the driver driver..
Therefore, Haryana Roadways would be liable to pay the compensation.
Thus, it was a clear cut case where the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of condition of insurance policy.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal has erred in fastening the liabili liability ty upon the appellant.

He has relied upon the judgments judgments passed by the Apex Court in case of another, (2020) AIR (SC) 4453 and Beli Ram versus Rajinder Kumar and another National Insurance Company Ltd. versus Vidhyadhar Mahariwala and others,,
(2008) AIR (SCW) 7145 wherein, it was held that in the absence of valid driving licence, the vehicle was being driven in breach of condition conditions of the insurance policy and thus, there is a breach of Section 149 (2) (a) (ii) of the M MACT ACT Act, the consequence being that the Insurance Insurance Company could not be held liable to pay the compensation.
6.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned for the respondent respondent-General General Manager, Haryana Roadways argues that it is not the responsibility of the employer and the learned Tribunal vide award dated 05.12.2006 has rightly held that if the driver of offending vehicle was holding a valid driving licence at the time when he was employed but the licence expired during the course of his employment employment, then the expiry of licence cannot be treated as a breach on the part of the owner of the vehicle.
Thereby the insurance company cannot escape from its liability to indemnify the insured.

Learned counsel for respondent No.4 submitted that respondent No.1 has placed on record copy of driving license Ex.R1, but the same is valid from 17.11.2004 to 16.11.2007 whereas the accident took place on 115.11.2004 5.11.2004 hence, on the date of alleged accident the respondent No.1 was not holding a valid driving license th thus us the Insurance (O&Mnational Insc. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and learned GP for respondents No.2 and 3 contended that since at the time of granting employment respondent No.1 was holdin holding g a valid vali driving license hence, Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability.

17. After er due consideration ooff the contention of the parties, I am of the view that the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability to indemnify the insured as has been held by Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court in case National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Chand Kaur and others others, 2006 ACJ 2183 it has been observed in this case law that if the driver 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132930 FAO-312-2007 2007 (O&M) -5- of offending vehicle was holding valid driving license when he was employed but license expired during the course of his employment then even if expiry of license be treated as breach on the part of the owner off the vehicle, the breach is not so fundamental as to have contributed to the cause of accident and in these circumstances the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the insured.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability to indemnify tthe insured.

Hence, nce, this issue is decided against respondent No.4 Insurance Company "
9.

This Court is satisfied with the reasoning of the learned Tribunal which held that company cannot escape from its liability to indemnify the insured, insured if the driver of the offending offending vehicle was holding a valid driving licence when he was employed but licence expired during the course of his employment.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rishi Pal Singh versus New India Assurance Co.
others, SLP (Civil) NO.24933 of 2019

Rishi Pal Singh versus New India Assurance Co.
others, SLP (Civil) NO.24933 of 2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held that the owner of the Ltd. and others, vehicle is expected to verify the driving skills and not run to the licensing authority to verify the genuineness of the driving licence before appointing a driver.

Therefore, once the owner is satisfied that the driver is ccompetent ompetent to drive the vehicle, it is not expected from the owner thereafter to verify the genuineness of the driving licence issued to the driver.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsu Road Transport Corporation versus National Insurance Company, Company 13 (9)
SCR 266 held as under:-
"8. In a claim for compensation, it is certainly open to the insurer under Section 149(2)(a)(ii) to take a defence that the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident was not duly 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132930 FAO-312-2007 2007 (O&M) -6- licensed.

entities.text:
Pepsu Road Transport Corporation versus National Insurance Company, Company 13 (9)
SCR 266
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Once such a defence is taken, tthe he onus is on the insurer.
But even after it is proved that the licence possessed by the driver was a fake one, whether there is liability on the insurer is the moot question.
As far as the owner of the vehicle is concerned, when he hires a driver, he has to check whether the driver has a valid driving licence.
Thereafter he has to satisfy himself as to the competence of the driver.

If satisfied in that regard also, it can be said that the owner had taken reasonable care in employing a person who is qualifi qualified ed and competent to (O&Mnational Insc. Comp vs Savitri Devi And Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12204539/
4 drive the vehicle.

entities.text: O&Mnational Insc. Comp vs Savitri Devi And Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The owner cannot be expected to go beyond that, to the extent of verifying the genuineness of the driving licence with the licensing authority before hiring the services of the driver.

However, the situation would be different if at the time of insurance of the vehicle or thereafter the insurance company requires the owner of the vehicle to have the licence duly verified from the licensing authority or if the attention of the owner of the vehicle is otherwise invited tto o the allegation that the licence issued to the driver employed by him is a fake one and yet the owner does not take appropriate action for verification of the matter regarding the genuineness of the licence from the licensing authority.
That is what is explained plained in Swaran Singh's case (supra).

If despite such information with the owner that the licence possessed by his driver is fake, no action is taken by the insured for appropriate verification, then the insured will be at fault and, in such 6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132930 FAO-312-2007 2007 (O&M) -7- circumstances, s, the insurance company is not liable for the compensation."
10. In view of the above, the present appeal is dismissed being devoid of any merit.
11. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
